title: Flow Watermark Governor: per-tenant backlog watermarking with staged slow-path and cross-fleet spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a Flow Watermark Governor that enforces tenant-level backlog watermarks and moves requests through a staged slow-path when fast-path headroom is saturated. The governor should enable controlled spillover into warm standby fleets, emit rich metrics for eviction and spill events, and cooperate with the autoscaler to avoid oscillation. Goal is to protect P95/P99 latency SLOs for high-priority customers while preserving predictable throughput guarantees for dedicated pools.
background: Current dedicated routing uses a single admission gate with per-tenant token buckets and a global queue. Under bursty traffic we observe cascading queue growth that raises P99 latency and causes noisy autoscaler churn. Prior tickets implemented token reservation and burst reservoirs, but we need a tenant-aware, multi-stage approach that reasons about backlog watermarks and coordinated spillover to secondary capacity to avoid global destabilization.
proposal: Add a Flow Watermark Governor component in the routing plane with three principal mechanisms: 1) Per-tenant watermarks (low/medium/high) computed from recent enqueue/dequeue rates and active KV cache hit ratios. 2) Staged slow-path: when watermark crosses thresholds, new requests are tagged for slow-path execution (aggressive batching, larger timeouts) with progressive demotion. 3) Cross-fleet spillover: when a tenant's high watermark persists and dedicated pool headroom is exhausted, the router performs controlled spillover to designated warm standby fleets or a burst pool with relaxed SLA, using tokenized permits and rate caps. The governor exposes backpressure signals to the autoscaler and applies a damped feedback loop to avoid flip-flopping.
technical_notes: Watermarks derived from exponential-weighted moving averages of enqueue rate, in-flight requests, and recent tail latency; configurable decay windows.
Slow-path behavior: 200ms batching window when demoted, optional KV cache bypass with a separate cache tier to reduce memory pressure, and micro-retries consolidated at proxy layer.

Spillover policy: allow <10% of peak tenant traffic to spill to warm pools by default, configurable per-customer; all spilled traffic is labeled and routed through a stricter token bucket with composable observability tags.

Autoscaler integration: governor emits HEADROOM_ESTIMATE and SPILLOVER_EVENT metrics consumed by autoscaler. Autoscaler must honor a 60s dampening window before scaling decisions influenced by spillover to reduce thrash.
SLO mapping: tenants with reserved throughput keep priority on the fast-path until sustained high-watermark duration > configured grace period (default 45s).
Failure modes: if warm pool unavailable, governor can toggle canary fallback to best-effort hosted model variants with a fallthrough bucket; must be auditable for billing reconciliation.

Infra: add metric exporters for per-tenant queue-length, watermark-state, spill_events (owner: Leo)
Runtime: implement governor admission check in router proxy and integrate demotion token (owner: Marco)

acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for priority tenants remains within 20% of baseline under 5x burst in dedicated pool with governor enabled
Governor emits WATERMARK_STATE and SPILLOVER_EVENT metrics with tenant tags and counts
Autoscaler respects HEADROOM_ESTIMATE metric with 60s dampening and does not oscillate in synthetic load test
Spillover volume is capped and observable; default spill cap enforced and configurable per-tenant
No increase in tail error rate for non-spilled priority requests above 0.2% during test scenarios
Runbook and dashboard published and stakeholders (SRE/PM/Account Exec) reviewed and approved
